/api/circulars/90001.subject: GRB 261017A: Swift detection of a burst
/api/circulars/90001.body:
At 16:05:05 UT, the Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) triggered and located GRB 261017A (trigger=1519536). Swift slewed immediately to the burst.

[Invented for the logbook fixture.]

/api/circulars/90002.subject: GRB 261017A: Swift-XRT refined analysis
/api/circulars/90002.body:
We have analysed 4.2 ks of XRT data for GRB 261017A. The light curve can be modelled with a power-law decay with an index of 1.1.

[Invented for the logbook fixture.]

/api/circulars/90003.subject: GRB 261017A: NOT optical upper limits
/api/circulars/90003.body:
We observed the field of GRB 261017A with the Nordic Optical Telescope, starting 4.9 h after the burst. No source is detected at the XRT position down to r > 23.1 (3 sigma).

[Invented for the logbook fixture.]

photometry.text: No source is detected at the XRT position down to r > 23.1 (3 sigma).

/api/circulars/90004.subject: GRB 261017A: GTC optical afterglow detection
/api/circulars/90004.body:
We observed the field of GRB 261017A with the 10.4 m GTC, 11 h after the burst. We detect a faint source at the XRT position, with r = 24.3 +/- 0.2.

[Invented for the logbook fixture.]

photometry.text: We detect a faint source at the XRT position, with r = 24.3 +/- 0.2.

/api/circulars/90005.subject: GRB 261017A: VLT/X-shooter spectroscopic redshift z = 0.42
/api/circulars/90005.body:
We obtained a spectrum of the afterglow of GRB 261017A with X-shooter. From several emission lines of the host galaxy we derive a redshift z = 0.42.

[Invented for the logbook fixture.]

/api/circulars/90006.subject: IceCube-261020A - IceCube observation of a high-energy neutrino candidate track-like event
/api/circulars/90006.body:
IceCube detected a track-like event with a moderate probability of being of astrophysical origin.

[Invented for the logbook fixture.]

/api/circulars/90007.subject: IceCube-261020A: ZTF optical upper limits
/api/circulars/90007.body:
We observed the localization region of IceCube-261020A with ZTF. No new transient is detected down to r > 20.5 within the 90 % region.

[Invented for the logbook fixture.]

photometry.text: No new transient is detected down to r > 20.5 within the 90 % region.

/api/circulars/90008.subject: LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA S261020fx: optical counterpart candidate FIX-KN-1
/api/circulars/90008.body:
We report the discovery of a fast-fading optical transient, FIX-KN-1, in the localisation of S261020fx. On 2026-10-21T08:10:00 UT we measure r = 20.6 +/- 0.1 (AB). In a second image, taken on 2026-10-22T08:20:00 UT, the source has faded to r = 21.5 +/- 0.2, and i > 22.1.

[Invented for the logbook fixture.]
